title: Business case: from metrics to money
summary: We measured what is measurable (scams and money paused, false pauses, reviews, analyst items, agent refusals), stated every other assumption with a range, and solved for break-even.

headline.label: Customers served instead of refused (agents, 2 test weeks)

sections.title: How many warned victims must stop for UVERA to pay for itself?
sections.lead: Instead of assuming a 30-70% follow rate, we solve for the break-even rate.

columns: break-even share of paused scam victims who stop

sections.takeaway: Break-even is 0.12% (base) and 5.1% with every assumption pessimistic. Published evidence: 12% of flagged payments abandoned at a real bank (NAB 2023); a randomised UK study cut scam payments from 22% to 4% with a risk-based warning and a cancel button (OBIE / Behaviouralist 2021).

sections.title: Net benefit per 1 million P2P transfers (synthetic test window, base assumptions)
sections.lead: Prevented = follow rate × scam money paused. Costs = false pauses (customer time, support, abandoned transfers) + 'not sure' reviews + servers.
sections.takeaway: Net benefit is positive at every follow rate tested, including 1%.

sections.title: Which assumption matters most? (net benefit at a 10% follow rate)
sections.lead: Each assumption moved from its low to its high value, one at a time.

x: support contact rate per false pause
customer minutes lost per false pause

sections.takeaway: No single assumption turns the net benefit negative.

sections.title: Agent service: customers no longer turned away
sections.lead: Every real cash-out request in the test days (19,301) replayed against the cash an agent holds.
sections.takeaway: 1,406 more customers served (41% fewer refusals) and Tk 10,472,100 of demand met, for Tk 4,920 more cash per agent-day. Field data: in Bangladesh 5% of agent transactions are denied for lack of float (Helix Institute).

caveats: Money figures are synthetic-world estimates per 1 million transfers; they show the economics are robust, not real savings.
Follow rates come from public studies of warnings in other markets; a controlled pilot must measure ours.
